r.정치 구도: A federal presidential system modeled on the United States, made up of 36 states and the capital territory of Abuja. To win the presidency, a candidate must not only top the national vote but also win more than 25% in at least two-thirds of the states, so no one can win with a single region. An unwritten rule that the presidency rotates between the Muslim north and the Christian south makes regional balance an issue from the moment parties pick their candidates. The government that took office in 2023 scrapped the fuel subsidy and let the currency float, sending prices sharply higher, and that pain is a central issue for the 2027 presidential election. The opposition is split into several camps and is negotiating over fielding a single candidate.

t.why: With well over 200 million people it is Africa's most populous country, and it is a member of OPEC. The Economic Community of West African States has its headquarters in Abuja, and Nigeria led the West African peacekeeping force during the civil wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone in the 1990s. Since Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso left the bloc in 2025, Nigeria's role in containing armed groups in the Sahel has grown. Boko Haram and Islamic State affiliates in the northeast, armed bandits in the northwest and clashes between farmers and herders in the middle belt all overlap. In 2025 the United States designated it a Country of Particular Concern for religious freedom, citing the persecution of Christians, and on Christmas Day struck Islamic State fighters in the northwest in cooperation with the Nigerian government.
t.rel: It borders Benin, Niger, Chad and Cameroon. With the countries around Lake Chad it formed a multinational force against armed groups such as Boko Haram. It disputed the Bakassi Peninsula with Cameroon and handed it over after an International Court of Justice ruling.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in 1980. Korea buys crude oil and natural gas and sells petrochemical products such as synthetic resins. Daewoo E&C has built gas processing facilities and liquefied natural gas plants there since the 1980s, and Samsung Heavy Industries built offshore oil production equipment at a joint-venture yard in Lagos. Samsung Electronics, LG Electronics and Lotte Chemical also operate there, and a Korean Cultural Center opened in 2010.
t.know: Nollywood ranks among the world's top film industries by the number of films made each year.
etext: It is one of Africa's leading oil producers and holds the continent's largest gas reserves. The giant Dangote refinery, running since 2024, is turning it from a petrol importer into a fuel exporter.
Its large and very young population has driven fast growth in telecoms, mobile payments, film and music. It is one of the African countries attracting the most startup investment.

Most government revenue and foreign currency come from oil, so falling oil prices hit it at once. Crude theft from pipelines and power shortages are severe, and since the 2023 reforms the naira has lost much of its value, keeping inflation high.
